examples.en: My little brother is a total grump.
The ill-tempered kid hid his friend's toy.
Why are you acting so grumpy today?

examples.ko: 할아버지는 장난이 심한 손자를 심술꾸러기라고 부르세요.
examples.en: Grandpa calls his grandson, who plays too many pranks, a little troublemaker.

examples.ko: 동화책에 나오는 심술꾸러기 왕이 마지막에 변했어요.
examples.en: The mean king in the storybook changed at the end.

examples.ko: 심술꾸러기가 웃는 모습은 오늘 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the grump smile for the first time today.

explain: '심술쟁이'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 아이나 가까운 사이에서 장난스럽게 놀릴 때 많이 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 강해요. '잠꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'는 그런 버릇이 있는 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '심술쟁이' and is often used playfully for children or close friends. If you say it to an adult, it sounds like teasing. Like '잠꾸러기' (sleepyhead), '-꾸러기' marks a person with that habit.

examples.en: My younger sibling suddenly threw a tantrum, and everyone was surprised.
When they are tired, kids keep acting up.
Why are you being mean only to me?

examples.ko: 심술부리지 말고 같이 놀자고 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't sulk. Try asking to play together.
He is not someone who gets sulky just because he loses.
The cat acted grumpy because its food was late.

explain: '심술을 부리다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요. 마음속에 심술이 생기는 건 '심술이 나다'이고, '심술부리다'는 그 마음을 겉으로 행동이나 말로 드러낸다는 느낌이에요. 아이나 반려동물, 친한 사람에게 자주 써요.
explain_en: You can also write it as '심술을 부리다'. '심술이 나다' means the grumpy feeling arises inside, while '심술부리다' means you show it through actions or words. It is often used for kids, pets and close people.

examples.ko: 우리 반 심술쟁이가 오늘은 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The grump of our class is smiling today.
The grumpy old man is actually the kindest.
If you act that spiteful, you won't have friends.
My younger sibling teases me by calling me a grump.
A mean witch appears in this cartoon.
Everyone knows who the grump is.

explain: '심술꾸러기'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말로, 심술을 잘 부리는 사람을 가볍게 놀리거나 부를 때 써요. '-쟁이'는 '욕심쟁이, 겁쟁이'처럼 그런 성격이나 버릇을 가진 사람에게 붙어요. 진짜 화가 났을 때보다는 장난스러운 말투에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used much like '심술꾸러기' to lightly tease someone who often acts spiteful. '-쟁이' attaches to a person with that trait, as in '욕심쟁이' (greedy person) and '겁쟁이' (coward). It fits a playful tone better than real anger.

examples.en: Try turning the screw with a Phillips screwdriver.
Please take a Phillips screwdriver out of the drawer.
I didn't have a Phillips screwdriver, so I opened it with a coin.
A Phillips screwdriver fits this screw.
My father always keeps the Phillips screwdriver in the toolbox.
We need to buy one Phillips and one flat-head screwdriver.

explain: 나사 머리가 '+' 모양이면 십자드라이버, '-' 모양이면 '일자드라이버'를 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '드라이버'라고 줄여 말하기도 해요. 머리카락 말리는 '드라이어'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: Use a 십자드라이버 for screws with a '+' head and a '일자드라이버' for a '-' head. In daily speech people often just say '드라이버'. Don't confuse it with '드라이어' (hair dryer).

examples.en: The numbers we use follow the decimal system.

examples.ko: 십진법에서는 열 개가 모이면 자리가 올라가요.
examples.en: In the decimal system, the next place begins once ten gather.
Computers use binary instead of the decimal system.
If you convert to the decimal system, the calculation is much easier.
We learned about the decimal system in math class today.
Please explain the difference between decimal and binary.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '이진법'이에요. '십진법으로 나타내다', '십진수'처럼 써요. 주로 수학이나 컴퓨터 수업에서 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '이진법' (binary). You will see it in phrases like '십진법으로 나타내다' and '십진수'. It mostly appears in math or computer classes, rarely in daily talk.

examples.en: The child grins after getting candy.
What's so good that you're grinning to yourself?
He worked all day with a grin on his face.
Don't just grin. Tell me the reason.
My younger sibling grinned when seeing my face.

examples.ko: 싱글거리는 모습을 보니 기분이 좋은가 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you grin, you must be in a good mood.

explain: 소리 내지 않고 눈과 입으로 부드럽게 웃는 모습이에요. 소리 내어 웃는 '깔깔거리다'와는 달라요. '싱글싱글 웃다'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a soft, silent smile with the eyes and mouth. It differs from '깔깔거리다', which is laughing out loud. People also often say '싱글싱글 웃다'.

examples.en: The kids are beaming because they are going on a picnic.
It's payday, so Dad has been beaming since morning.
She beamed after receiving the gift.
Why are you beaming since this morning?
You came in with a beaming face, so I knew everything.
She did well on the exam, so she will be beaming.

explain: '싱글거리다'보다 기분이 좋아서 계속 웃는 느낌이 더 강해요. '싱글벙글 웃다'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요. 아이, 가족, 친구처럼 가까운 사람의 밝은 표정을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '싱글거리다', it more strongly suggests someone keeps smiling because they are happy. It is also very common as an adverb, as in '싱글벙글 웃다'. It suits the bright expression of kids, family or friends.

examples.en: Now that it's spring, my mind feels restless.
My friends are getting married, and I feel unsettled for no reason.

examples.ko: 오늘은 일이 손에 안 잡히고 싱숭생숭했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't focus on work today and felt restless.

examples.ko: 마음이 싱숭생숭해서 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My mind was unsettled, so I couldn't sleep all night.
Feeling restless, I went out for a walk alone.
Why does my mind feel so unsettled?

explain: 슬프다기보다 마음이 들떠서 어수선하고 차분하지 않은 상태에 써요. 보통 '마음이 싱숭생숭하다'처럼 마음과 같이 말하고, '싱숭생숭해지다'로 변화도 나타내요. 봄이나 큰 변화 앞에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes a mind that is unsettled and hard to calm, more than simply sad. It usually goes with '마음', as in '마음이 싱숭생숭하다', and '싱숭생숭해지다' shows the change. It often appears in spring or before big changes.

examples.en: A little graupel fell this morning.
Snow grains are falling with a rustle outside the window.
The snow grains piled up and the road turned white.
Snow grains blown by the wind hit my face.
Snow grains will come tonight.
It was fine snow rather than big flakes, so it stopped soon.

explain: 쌀알처럼 작고 단단한 눈이에요. 크고 푹신하게 내리는 '함박눈'과 대비해서 기억하면 좋아요. 주로 겨울 날씨 이야기나 글에서 나와요.
explain_en: It is small, hard snow like grains of rice. It helps to remember it as the opposite of '함박눈', big fluffy snow. It mostly appears in winter weather talk and writing.

examples.en: That friend was a well-known brawler in the neighborhood.
He looks like a fighter, but he is actually soft-hearted.
The quarrelsome man is quiet today.
I am not a fighter but a peace lover.
The fighter in the movie looked so cool.
You must not get in between the fighters.

explain: '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 자주 하거나 잘하는 사람에게 붙어요. 싸움꾼은 싸움을 잘하거나 자주 하는 사람이라 칭찬보다는 조금 부정적인 느낌이에요. 말다툼을 자주 하는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '-꾼' attaches to a person who often does or is good at something. A 싸움꾼 is someone who fights well or often, so it sounds a bit negative rather than praising. It can also be used for someone who often argues.

examples.en: Young soldiers left for a distant battlefield.
I heard the story of my father who came back from the battlefield.
These days the office feels like a battleground every day.
This place was a big battleground long ago.
I went to the exam hall with the mindset of going to battle.

examples.ko: 시장이 싸움터가 된 것을 보고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was shocked to see the market turned into a battleground.

explain: '전쟁터'와 비슷하게 쓰이지만 비유로도 자주 써요. '회사는 싸움터다', '시험장은 싸움터다'처럼 경쟁이 치열한 곳을 말할 수 있어요. 실제 전투를 말할 때는 '전쟁터'가 더 일반적으로 들려요.
explain_en: It is used much like '전쟁터' but also works figuratively. You can say '회사는 싸움터다' for any fiercely competitive place. For real warfare, '전쟁터' sounds more common.

examples.en: If you boil soup with rice water, it tastes nutty and rich.
Don't throw away the rice water. Save it.
My mother dissolves soybean paste in rice water.
Radish boiled in rice water tastes good.
Can I give rice water to plants?

examples.ko: 쌀뜨물이 뽀얗게 나올 때까지 쌀을 씻어요.
examples.en: I wash the rice until the rice water comes out milky.

explain: 쌀을 씻을 때 나오는 뽀얀 물이에요. 된장국이나 찌개 국물을 낼 때 쓰는 집도 많아요. '쌀뜨물'이라고 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is the milky water that comes out when you wash rice. Many households use it as a base for soybean paste soup or stews. It is written as one word, '쌀뜨물'.

examples.ko: 쌀통 바닥에 쌀알이 조금 남아 있어요.
examples.en: A few grains of rice are left at the bottom of the rice bin.
The rice grains are plump, so the rice tastes good.
Each grain of this rice is long and slender.
Rice grains have fallen on the kitchen floor.
Birds peck at the rice grains in the yard.
When you cook porridge, the rice grains gradually swell.

explain: 익히지 않은 쌀의 낱알은 '쌀알', 지은 밥의 낱알은 '밥알'이라고 구분해요. 그래서 밥 먹다가 말할 때는 보통 '밥알'을 써요. 소리 나는 대로 [싸랄]이라고 읽어요.
explain_en: A single uncooked grain is a '쌀알', while a grain of cooked rice is a '밥알'. So when talking about eating a meal, people usually say '밥알'. It is pronounced [싸랄].

examples.en: This tea tastes a little bitter.
A slightly bitter coffee is perfect in the morning.
I like dark chocolate because it is pleasantly bitter.

examples.ko: 쌉쌀한 맛 때문에 아이들은 안 먹어요.
examples.en: Kids don't eat it because of the bitter taste.
It is bitter at first, but sweet afterward.

examples.ko: 녹차를 너무 쌉쌀하지 않게 우려 주세요.
examples.en: Please brew the green tea so it isn't too bitter.

explain: '쓰다'보다 약하고, 싫지 않은 쓴맛이라는 느낌으로 써요. 커피, 차, 초콜릿, 나물 같은 음식 맛을 말할 때 잘 나와요. 칭찬하는 말투로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is milder than '쓰다' and suggests a bitterness that is not unpleasant. It often describes coffee, tea, chocolate and wild greens. People often use it in a positive tone.

examples.en: I packed binoculars to watch birds.
Through binoculars, the mountain looks close.
Many people use binoculars at concerts.
Can you lend me your binoculars?

examples.ko: 아이가 쌍안경으로 별을 보고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants to look at stars with binoculars.
The binoculars are heavy, so my neck hurts.

explain: 두 눈으로 함께 보는 망원경이에요. '망원경'은 더 넓은 말이고, 쌍안경은 그중 두 눈으로 보는 종류예요. '쌍안경을 쓰다', '쌍안경으로 보다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a telescope-like device you look through with both eyes. '망원경' is the broader word, and 쌍안경 is the two-eyed kind. You say '쌍안경을 쓰다' or '쌍안경으로 보다'.

examples.en: I have to write and hand in the report by tomorrow.
It took two days to write and submit the application.
I wrote down all the answers on the exam paper.
The teacher told us to write and hand in a reflection.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 한 달 만에 소설을 써냈어요.
examples.en: That person wrote out a novel in a month.
If you just write your name and submit, the application is done.

explain: '써서 내다'가 합쳐진 말로, 서류나 답안을 써서 제출한다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '소설을 써내다'처럼 글을 완성해 내놓는 뜻도 있어요. 그냥 제출만 할 때는 '내다'나 '제출하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It combines '써서 내다' and is often used for writing a document or answer and handing it in. It can also mean completing and producing a piece of writing, as in '소설을 써내다'. For just submitting, use '내다' or '제출하다'.

examples.en: My friend got angry and snapped at me.
Don't snap like that. Talk calmly.
My younger sibling snapped at Mom and went into the room.
He always speaks in a snappy tone.
I'm really sorry for snapping at you for no reason earlier.
I saw a customer snapping at a staff member.

explain: 상대에게 날카롭고 퉁명스럽게 한마디 쏘듯이 말할 때 써요. '나무라다'보다 감정이 담긴 말투를 말해요. '쏘아붙이듯 말하다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: It means to say something sharp and blunt to someone, as if shooting words. It focuses more on an emotional tone than '나무라다' (to scold). You can also say '쏘아붙이듯 말하다'.

examples.en: If you put crown daisy in the stew, it smells nice.
Crown daisy has a strong scent, so people either love or hate it.
I bought a bunch of crown daisy at the market.
I blanched the crown daisy lightly and seasoned it.
Fish cake soup feels lacking without crown daisy.
I eat crown daisy and lettuce together as a wrap.

explain: 이름에 '쑥'이 들어가지만 쑥과는 다른 채소예요. 탕, 찌개, 쌈에 향을 더하려고 넣는 경우가 많아요. 받침 ㅅ이 [ㄷ]으로 소리 나서 발음은 [쑥깓]이에요.
explain_en: Although it has '쑥' in its name, it is a different vegetable from mugwort. It is often added to soups, stews and wraps for aroma. The final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ, so it is pronounced [쑥깓].

examples.en: It stings when I put disinfectant on the wound.
I fell, and my knee keeps stinging.
After the breakup, my heart ached a lot.
The painful experience made me stronger.
My back is sore from sunburn.
My eyes stung, so tears came out.

explain: '쓰리다'는 '배가 쓰리다'처럼 속이 아플 때도 쓰지만, '쓰라리다'는 쓸리거나 데인 상처가 쓰리고 아린 느낌이에요. 마음에 쓰면 '쓰라린 패배'처럼 괴롭고 아픈 경험을 말해요. '쓰라린'으로 명사를 꾸미는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '쓰리다' can describe an upset stomach, as in '배가 쓰리다', but '쓰라리다' is the stinging, smarting feeling of a scraped or burned wound. For the mind, it means a painful experience, as in '쓰라린 패배'. It is often used before a noun as '쓰라린'.

examples.en: I swept the dust into the dustpan.
The broom and dustpan are next to the entrance.
The dustpan broke, so I bought a new one.
The child held the dustpan for me.
I carefully cleaned up the glass pieces with a dustpan.
Could you bring me the dustpan?

explain: 보통 '빗자루'와 한 쌍으로 기억하면 좋아요. 쓸어 모은 먼지나 쓰레기를 받아서 담는 도구예요. 발음은 [쓰레받끼]예요.
explain_en: It is easiest to remember as a pair with '빗자루' (broom). It is the tool that catches the swept dust or trash. It is pronounced [쓰레받끼].

examples.en: He slipped past in front of me.
I drew a line across the paper in one stroke.
I wiped the sweat away with my hand.
I just glanced over it, and the answer showed up.
The child came up quietly and said hello.
As soon as the knife touched it, the fruit was cut smoothly.

explain: '슥'보다 조금 센 느낌으로, 손이나 몸이 가볍게 한 번에 스치듯 움직일 때 써요. '쓱 닦다', '쓱 지나가다', '쓱 훑어보다'처럼 동작 앞에 붙여요. 여러 번 반복하면 '쓱쓱'이에요.
explain_en: It feels a little stronger than '슥' and is used when a hand or body moves lightly in one swipe. It goes before an action, as in '쓱 닦다', '쓱 지나가다' and '쓱 훑어보다'. Repeated, it becomes '쓱쓱'.

examples.en: He shook his head with a wry smile.
All I could manage was a bitter smile at the news of failure.
It was so absurd that a wry smile came out.
I gave a forced smile at my friend's joke.
A faint bitter smile spread across his face.
Sadness was hidden behind the wry smile.

explain: 기쁘지 않거나 어이없을 때 억지로 짓는 웃음이에요. '쓴웃음을 짓다', '쓴웃음이 나다'처럼 자주 말해요. 맛이 쓰다는 뜻이 아니라 마음이 개운하지 않은 웃음이에요.
explain_en: It is a smile you force when you are not happy or find something absurd. It is often said as '쓴웃음을 짓다' or '쓴웃음이 나다'. It has nothing to do with taste, but with a smile that leaves a sour feeling.

examples.en: I threw away the stuff I had piled up for no use.
I don't want to spend my time uselessly.
It's a bag that's just big and useless.
That money disappeared to no purpose.

examples.ko: 가끔은 내가 쓸모없이 느껴지는 날도 있어요.
examples.en: Some days I feel useless.
Don't just worry pointlessly. Let's move.

explain: '쓸모없다'의 부사형으로, 도움이 안 되거나 낭비되는 모습을 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '쓸모 있게'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 심하게 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '쓸모없다' and describes something unhelpful or wasted. The opposite feeling is '쓸모 있게'. Be careful with people, as it can sound harsh.

examples.en: I swept all the leaves in the yard away with a broom.
A huge flood swept away the small village.
I feel refreshed after sweeping away the dust.
The kids polished off the snacks in no time.
Let's sweep away all our worries and start fresh.
I sweep up the hair on the floor in one go.

explain: '쓸다'에 '-어 버리다'가 붙어 깨끗이 없애 버린다는 느낌이 강해요. 먼지뿐 아니라 홍수나 태풍이 휩쓸어 가는 것, 음식을 다 먹어 치우는 것에도 비유로 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 거친 말이 되니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It adds '-어 버리다' to '쓸다', giving a strong feeling of clearing something away completely. Beyond dust, it is used for floods or storms sweeping things off and, figuratively, for eating up food. Used about people, it becomes a rough expression.

examples.ko: 이 고기는 질겨서 잘 안 씹혀요.
examples.en: This meat is tough, so it doesn't chew easily.
I bit my tongue while eating.
I was surprised when I felt grit crunching in my mouth.
I like the crunchy bite of it.
This squid is chewy, so it tastes good.
It's a restaurant where the meat is tender to chew.

explain: '씹다'는 내가 하는 동작이고, '씹히다'는 음식이 입안에서 어떻게 느껴지는지 말해요. '잘 씹히다', '질겨서 안 씹히다'처럼 식감을 나타내요. 먹다가 모래나 혀가 뜻하지 않게 씹히는 경우에도 써요.
explain_en: '씹다' is the action you do, while '씹히다' describes how food feels in your mouth. It expresses texture, as in '잘 씹히다' and '질겨서 안 씹히다'. It also covers grit or your tongue getting bitten unexpectedly.

examples.en: On the downhill road, the bike zooms along.
The wind is whistling hard, so it's really cold.
Cars whiz by on the highway.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈 위에서 씽씽 썰매를 타요.
examples.en: The child zips along on a sled over the snow.
I read a book on the speeding train.
A motorcycle whizzed past me.

explain: 무언가가 빠르게 달리거나 바람이 세게 불 때 쓰는 말이에요. '쌩쌩'과 느낌이 비슷해요. 속도가 시원스럽게 빠르다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for something moving fast or wind blowing strongly. The feel is similar to '쌩쌩'. It carries a sense of brisk, refreshing speed.

examples.en: Fish breathe through their gills.
If the fish's gills are red, it is fresh.
I removed the gills and prepared the fish.

examples.ko: 물 밖에 나온 물고기가 아가미를 뻐끔거려요.
examples.en: The fish out of water gulps with its gills.
The fish got hurt because the net caught on its gills.

examples.ko: 손질할 때 아가미 쪽에 칼을 넣어요.
examples.en: When preparing it, I put the knife in near the gills.

explain: 물고기가 물속에서 숨 쉬는 기관이에요. 사람이 숨 쉬는 '폐'와 짝지어 기억하면 쉬워요. 생선을 살 때 아가미 색을 보고 신선한지 확인하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the organ fish use to breathe underwater. It helps to pair it with '폐' (lungs), which humans use to breathe. When buying fish, people sometimes check the gill color to see if it is fresh.

examples.en: Friendships are important in childhood.
He had a difficult childhood.
Habits from childhood last a lifetime.
Childhood and adolescence differ in growth speed.
I wrote about my childhood experiences.
It's good to read a lot of books in childhood.

explain: 유아기 다음, 청소년기 앞의 시기를 말하는 학술적인 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '어린 시절'이나 '어렸을 때'라고 해요. 교육, 심리, 뉴스 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat academic word for the period after infancy and before adolescence. In daily talk, people usually say '어린 시절' or '어렸을 때'. It often appears in education, psychology and news writing.

examples.en: My boy is already a middle schooler.
I'm worried these days because of my boy.
My boy came home with an award from school.
The son of that family greets people well.
I gave my boy a little pocket money.
It's my boy's birthday, so I cooked seaweed soup.

explain: 아들을 친근하고 편하게, 조금 낮춰 부르는 구어체 말이에요. 주로 부모님이나 이웃 어른이 말해요. 공식적인 자리에서는 '아들'을 쓰고, 남의 아들을 높일 때는 '아드님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a casual, affectionate and slightly humble spoken word for a son. Parents and neighborhood adults mostly use it. In formal situations use '아들', and to respectfully refer to someone else's son, say '아드님'.

examples.en: My lower tooth was loose, so I went to the dentist.
One of my lower teeth fell out yesterday.
The child laughs showing the lower teeth.
My lower and upper teeth don't fit together well.
It hurts a bit when I brush my lower teeth.
I had a lower tooth pulled at the dentist.

explain: 반대말은 '윗니'예요. 소리 나는 대로 [아랜니]라고 읽어요. 이가 빠졌을 때 아이에게는 '아랫니'와 '윗니'를 나눠 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '윗니' (upper tooth). It is pronounced [아랜니]. People often distinguish '아랫니' and '윗니', for example when a child loses a tooth.

examples.en: The hem of these pants is too long.
I want to shorten the hem of the skirt.
It rained, so the bottom hem got muddy.
The dry cleaner altered the hem for me.
The bottom of my jeans is all worn out.
If I fold up the hem, it fits perfectly.

explain: 바지나 치마의 아래쪽 끝부분을 말해요. '밑단'이라고도 해요. 옷을 수선할 때 '아랫단을 줄이다, 늘리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the bottom edge of pants or a skirt. It is also called '밑단'. When tailoring, you say '아랫단을 줄이다' (shorten) or '늘리다' (lengthen).

en: warmest part of an ondol floor

examples.en: In winter, the warmest part of the floor is the best.
Grandmother spread the blanket on the warm part of the floor.
I sat on the warm spot of the floor and ate tangerines.
The warm spot is too hot, so I can't sit there.
The children gathered on the warm part of the floor.
I tucked the rice bowl under the blanket on the warm spot of the floor.

explain: 온돌방에서 불을 때는 곳과 가까워 바닥이 가장 따뜻한 쪽이에요. 반대말은 '윗목'이에요. 겨울에 가족이 이불 속에 발을 넣고 모이던 장면과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In an ondol room, it is the part of the floor closest to the heat source and warmest. Its opposite is '윗목'. It often appears in scenes of family gathering with their feet under a blanket in winter.

examples.en: I exercise with dumbbells every morning.

examples.ko: 집에서 쓸 아령 두 개를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two dumbbells for home use.
If I hold dumbbells for long, my arms hurt.
I start with three-kilogram dumbbells.
Dumbbell exercises are good to do at home.
I put down the dumbbells and rested for a moment.

explain: 헬스장에서는 영어 외래어로 '덤벨'이라고도 많이 말해요. '아령 운동'이나 '아령을 들다'처럼 써요. 팔 힘을 기르는 작은 운동 기구예요.
explain_en: At the gym, people also often say the loanword '덤벨'. You say '아령 운동' or '아령을 들다'. It is a small piece of equipment for building arm strength.

examples.en: The question was unclear, so I couldn't answer.
I'm not sure what that statement means.
He looked at me with a puzzled expression.

examples.ko: 기억이 아리송해서 확실하게 말 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: My memory is hazy, so I can't say for sure.
The more I read this problem, the more confusing it was.

examples.ko: 아리송하게 말하지 말고 분명히 말해 줘요.
examples.en: Don't be vague. Tell me clearly.

explain: 뜻이나 기억이 분명하지 않아서 헷갈릴 때 써요. 일상에서는 '헷갈려요'라고 더 많이 말하고, 아리송하다는 약간 부드럽고 글 같은 느낌이에요. '기억이 아리송하다', '표정이 아리송하다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when meaning or memory is unclear and confusing. In daily talk people more often say '헷갈려요', and 아리송하다 feels slightly softer and more written. It often appears in '기억이 아리송하다' and '표정이 아리송하다'.

en: whoops; oh my goodness; oh my gosh

examples.en: Oh my goodness, you appeared out of nowhere and startled me!
Oh my gosh, I left my wallet at home!

examples.ko: 아이고머니, 이 가방이 정말 이만 원이에요?
examples.en: Oh my goodness, is this bag really twenty thousand won?
Oh my, is it raining this hard?
Whoops, I stepped on your foot. I'm sorry!
Oh my goodness, this is bad. What do I do!

explain: 놀라거나 당황했을 때 나오는 감탄사로, '아이고'나 '어머나'와 비슷해요. 말투가 조금 옛스럽고 정겨운 느낌이라 친한 사이나 가벼운 상황에서 어울려요. 아주 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is an exclamation for surprise or flustered moments, similar to '아이고' or '어머나'. It sounds a bit old-fashioned and warm, so it suits close relationships and light situations. It is rarely used in very formal settings.
